title: a subscript of a struct that declares __getitem__ and __setitem__, on the left of and/or, calls the getter twice when it decides
compiler: prints `get 0`, `get 0`, `True`, at the default level and -O0: the getter runs to test the operand and again for the result. With a setter the index's values also live until after the getter when the subscript does not decide, and a getter that takes its index `var` is rejected, since its second call uses the temporary the first consumed
fixed: calls the getter once, with the destroy order of the same struct without __setitem__, so it prints `get 0`, `True`; the human ruled the destroy order and the consumed index part of the bug on 2026-11-21

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular
